title: Resources hub — RFID & NFC guides, comparisons and vendor compatibility
summary: Three ways into the catalog from one page. Read the Guides if you're learning the technology — chip-family encyclopedias, protocol references and regulation explainers. Use the Compare pages once you've shortlisted two or three options and need a head-to-head decision. Open the Compatibility pages when you've chosen the lock or reader estate and need to know exactly which RFID/NFC card encodes for it. Every page is written by working RFID engineers, cites the underlying standard or spec sheet, and links straight to the matching Proud Tek SKU.
heroPoints: Guides — chip-family encyclopedias (NTAG21x, NTAG424 DNA, MIFARE, ICODE, EM4x00, UCODE), air-interface protocols and clause-by-clause regulation explainers, for when you're scoping what's possible.
Compare — head-to-head decision matrices (chip vs chip, HF vs UHF, reader vs reader, RFID vs barcode) for narrowing a shortlist and defending it to procurement.
Compatibility — vendor cross-references naming the exact chip family and Proud Tek SKU each hotel-lock estate encodes for (Saflok, VingCard, Onity, MIWA, Salto, Häfele, Be-Tech).
Every resource cites the underlying ISO / GS1 / FDA / EU standard or the NXP / Impinj / Alien spec sheet — and links straight to the matching SKU, so you move from concept to sample in two clicks.

sections.title: Which resource do I need?
sections.intro: Most projects pass through all three over their life. Start with the one that matches your question today.
bullets: Learning the technology? Start in [Guides](/guides/) — chip-family encyclopedias, protocol internals and clause-by-clause regulation explainers for scoping what's possible.
Narrowing a shortlist? Go to [Compare](/compare/) — feature matrices with a 'pick X if … pick Y if …' call for chip, frequency-band, form-factor and reader decisions.
Already chose the lock, reader or PMS? Open [Compatibility](/compatibility/) — it names the exact chip family and Proud Tek SKU each estate encodes for.
Still deciding whether RFID is even right? Compare weighs RFID against barcode, QR and BLE before you commit to the technology at all.

faq.question: How often are these resources updated?
faq.answer: Each resource has a `publishedAt` and `modifiedAt` date stamp at the bottom of the page (and in the JSON-LD Article markup). Chip-family encyclopedias and protocol guides are updated when the chip vendor publishes a new datasheet revision or the standards body issues an amendment. Regulation explainers (EU DPP, FDA DSCSA, Walmart mandate) are updated when the underlying regulation, mandate or implementation guidance changes. Compare and compatibility pages are reviewed annually and whenever a new chip family or lock estate enters the field.

faq.question: Why do you cite specific clauses of standards?
faq.answer: Procurement teams audit RFID vendor claims against the underlying regulation. A clause-by-clause citation (ISO/IEC 14443-3:2018 §6.3, ISO/IEC 18000-63 §6.3.1.2.5, GS1 EPC TDS 2.0 §16.1, EU DPP draft delegated act Annex IV) lets the buyer's compliance team trace the claim to source rather than trust a marketing summary. The Resources hub is the same content the Proud Tek engineering team reads internally — written for engineers, audited by procurement.

faq.question: Can I copy and paste from these resources for an internal RFP or specification?
faq.answer: Yes. The resources are written in a style optimised for RFP / spec-sheet authoring — short numbered points, citation-by-clause, side-by-side decision matrices, pricing envelopes per chip and form factor. You're welcome to lift the comparison tables and chip-family reference content directly into your internal documents. We only ask for a backlink if the resource ends up published on a public page (blog post, conference paper, vendor selection deck shared externally).
